Empirical Research Plan: Long-Run Impacts of Teacher Value-Added

-------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
-------------------------------------------------
Strategy:  “Teacher-switch” event study combined with a within–school-by-grade-by-year (SGY) quasi-random assignment design.  

• Step 1 (first stage):  Estimate leave-one-year-out teacher value-added (VA) in math and English using only test-score data that precede the focal cohort.  
• Step 2 (reduced form):  Exploit the idiosyncratic year-to-year movement of teachers across SGY cells.  When a high-VA teacher arrives (or departs), average contemporaneous test scores of that grade in that school jump (or fall).  Treat these discrete “shocks” as a plausibly exogenous source of variation in the quality of instruction to which a given cohort is exposed.  
• Step 3 (second stage):  Use the predicted change in teacher VA generated by Step 2 as an instrument for actual teacher VA received by a student and relate it to adult outcomes observed in the tax data.  

Formally, our preferred specification is a two-stage least squares event-study / shift-share IV:

1st stage (exposure):
 TeacherVA_{c} = π · Predicted_TeacherVA_Shift_{sgy} + γ_{sgy} + λ_{g} + X_{isc}β + ε_{isc}

2nd stage (outcome):
 Y_{isc} = α · ŤeacherVA_{c} + γ_{sgy} + λ_{g} + X_{isc}β + υ_{isc}

where  
• i = student, s = school, g = grade, y = year, c = classroom.  
• γ_{sgy} = school-by-grade-by-year fixed effect (compares classmates within the same SGY).  
• λ_{g} = grade fixed effects.  
• X_{isc} includes gender, race, FRPL status, lagged test scores, and parent covariates.  

Why appropriate?  
1. Large panel lets us obtain precise pre-period VA estimates for every teacher.  
2. Teachers flow in/out for reasons unrelated to a single cohort, generating quasi-random variation in exposure.  
3. SGY fixed effects purge all school-grade-year demand-side factors (principal leadership, curricular reforms, neighborhood shocks).  
4. Event-study plots allow transparent validation: test-score levels move exactly in the year a teacher arrives/departs, not before.  


-------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
-------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable:  Continuous measure – teacher value-added in test scores, standardized to mean 0, SD = 1 across the district.  In some specifications we bin into quintiles; “treated” = teacher in top quintile (≥ 0.67 SD above mean).

Control group:  Students in the same school, grade, and year taught by teachers with lower VA (or in bottom quintile when using the binary treatment).

Treatment timing / event date:  The first year a new teacher is assigned to a SGY cell (arrival) or the first year after she leaves (departure).  Cohorts taught in those years are “exposed”; those in adjacent years act as pre- and post- cohorts in the event study.

No running variable → no RDD required.


-------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
-------------------------------------------------
A1. Within-SGY random assignment.  Conditional on SGY fixed effects and observables, students are as-good-as randomly allocated across teachers in a grade.  
• Plausible:  District does not allow parental selection of individual teachers; class lists finalized centrally.

A2. Teacher turnover unrelated to unobserved, cohort-specific shocks to long-run outcomes.  
• Plausible:  Turnover driven mainly by maternity leaves, relocations, retirements; not by information about the incoming cohort.

A3. Pre-period VA is a stable, unbiased measure of teacher quality (i.e., attenuation bias only from measurement error).  
• Supported by literature; we will implement empirical validity checks.

A4. No general-equilibrium spillovers across grades or schools that differentially follow teacher moves.  
• Testable by checking unaffected grades within the same school.

A5. Stable unit treatment value (SUTVA):  A student’s adult outcomes depend only on her own teacher, not the assignment of peers to teachers in other classes.  
• Reasonable given classroom separation; we will probe via leave-one-out peer exposure tests.


-------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
-------------------------------------------------
Threat 1: Non-random student sorting within SGY (e.g., principals place higher achievers with star teachers).  
• Mitigation:   
  – Include prior-year (t-1) math & ELA scores and their interactions with grade dummies;  
  – Balance tests: Regress lagged scores and demographics on teacher VA within SGY; coefficients should be ≈ 0.  
  – Replicate results using only schools that explicitly randomize (“simple lottery” scheduling sub-sample).

Threat 2: Measurement error in VA induces attenuation; could also bias IV if predictive power weak.  
• Mitigation:  
  – Use empirical Bayes shrinkage in VA estimation;  
  – Rely on large pre-sample (≈10 yrs) to improve signal-to-noise;  
  – Report first-stage F-stats > 10; cluster SEs at teacher level.

Threat 3: Incomplete tax-data linkage and selective migration out of state.  
• Mitigation:  
  – Show balance of baseline covariates between matched vs. unmatched students;  
  – Inverse-probability weights based on propensity to match;  
  – Robustness: restrict to students observed in any W-2 record by age 25 (stable subsample).


-------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
-------------------------------------------------
```r
############################################################
# 0.  Libraries
############################################################
library(data.table)    # fast I/O
library(fixest)        # high-dimensional FE + IV
library(ggplot2)

############################################################
# 1.  Load data
############################################################
# Assume csv files in working directory
students   <- fread("student_panel.csv")   # student-subject-year
teachers   <- fread("teacher_va.csv")      # teacher id, pre-period VA
events     <- fread("teacher_switches.csv")# SGY-level VA shocks

############################################################
# 2.  Merge and construct variables
############################################################
# a) Attach teacher VA to student records
students <- merge(students, teachers[, .(teacher_id, va_std)], 
                  by = "teacher_id", all.x = TRUE)

# b) Attach predicted shift: mean entering VA minus leaving VA in SGY
students <- merge(students, events[, .(school_id, grade, year, va_shift_std)], 
                  by = c("school_id","grade","year"), all.x = TRUE)

# c) Adult outcomes (earnings at 28)
students[, earn28 := fifelse(age == 28, earnings, NA_real_), 
         by = "student_id"]
# Keep one obs per student (or run at classroom level)
analysis <- students[!is.na(earn28)]

# d) Lagged test scores (grade-specific)
analysis[, lag_math := shift(math_z, 1, type = "lag"), 
         by = student_id]
analysis[, lag_ela  := shift(ela_z, 1, type = "lag"), 
         by = student_id]

############################################################
# 3.  Main IV regression: adult earnings on teacher VA
############################################################
fe_formula <- earn28 ~ 1 | school_id^grade^year + gender + race + 
                       lag_math + lag_ela + parent_income_05_07

iv_model <- feols(fe_formula, analysis, 
                  iv = ~ va_std | va_shift_std,     # 2SLS
                  cluster = "teacher_id")           # cluster at teacher

summary(iv_model)

############################################################
# 4.  Event-study plot for contemporaneous test scores
############################################################
# Estimate year-relative effects around teacher arrival
event <- feols(math_z ~ i(rel_year, ref = -1) | school_id^grade + teacher_id, 
               data = events_long)   # events_long has ±5yr window
iplot(event) + labs(y = "Math Z-score", x = "Years relative to arrival")

############################################################
# 5.  Robustness:  restrict to random-assignment schools
############################################################
iv_rand <- feols(fe_formula, 
                 analysis[randomized == 1], 
                 iv = ~ va_std | va_shift_std, 
                 cluster = "teacher_id")
etable(iv_model, iv_rand)
```

Notes:  
• school_id^grade^year in fixest creates saturated SGY fixed effects.  
• The first-stage can be viewed with summary(iv_model, stage = 1).  


-------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
-------------------------------------------------
Direction:  Positive.  Being taught by a 1 SD higher-VA teacher in a single grade should raise adult (age 28) annual W-2 earnings by roughly 1–2 % (≈ \$250–\$500 on a \$25,000 base), increase college attendance by ~0.5 pp, shift students into ~2 % higher-quartile colleges, move adult residence to neighborhoods with ~1 pt higher income-rank, raise 401(k) participation by ~0.3 pp, and lower teen birth by ~0.3 pp.  Economic theory of human-capital accumulation plus prior test-score evidence point to small but meaningful lifetime gains; compounding across 13 years of schooling magnifies to ≈ \$10k–\$20k present-value per student.


-------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (Event-Study / Teacher-Switch IV)
-------------------------------------------------
C1: No systematic student sorting within SGY ………………… 0.8  
C2: Teacher turnover unrelated to cohort shocks ……………… 0.8  
C3: Stable pre-trend in outcomes (event-study flat pre-t) …… 0.9  
C4: First-stage relevance (F > 10) ………………………………… 1  
C5: No spillovers/contamination across units ………………… 0.7  

Overall score ≈ 4.2 / 5.
